questions.question: What is the best initial approach to new lower urinary tract symptoms?
choices: Assume BPH and prescribe medication immediately
Characterize storage and voiding symptoms, review medications, assess red flags, and perform appropriate evaluation
Treat every symptom as a UTI
Order a medication refill without history
questions.explanation: LUTS have many causes. A focused history, examination, urinalysis and selected further assessment help distinguish BPH, infection, overactive bladder, retention, medication effects, and serious disease.

questions.question: Which alpha-blocker adverse effect is especially important in a patient with recent falls?
choices: Orthostatic hypotension or syncope
Improved urinary flow
Lower medication cost
Increased bone density
questions.explanation: Alpha blockers can improve symptoms but may cause dizziness, orthostatic hypotension, and syncope, particularly with other antihypertensives or vulnerable volume status.

questions.question: Why should cataract-surgery history be reviewed before alpha-blocker treatment?
choices: It determines the UTI antibiotic choice
Some alpha blockers are associated with intraoperative floppy iris syndrome
It proves a prostate diagnosis
It eliminates fall risk
questions.explanation: Alpha blockers can be associated with intraoperative floppy iris syndrome. Patients and eye surgeons need an accurate medication history.

questions.question: What is a key limitation of treating urgency with an antimuscarinic medication without further assessment?
choices: It always cures urinary retention
It can worsen constipation, cognition, falls, blurred vision, or urinary retention in susceptible patients
It prevents all UTIs
It has no systemic effects
questions.explanation: Antimuscarinics can carry anticholinergic adverse effects. The cause of urgency and patient-specific cognitive, bowel, fall, and retention risk matter.

questions.question: Why does erectile dysfunction warrant a broader health assessment?
choices: It is never related to medical illness
It can be associated with vascular disease, diabetes, hypertension, medications, endocrine disease, and other conditions
It is treated safely with every medication
It does not affect function or quality of life
questions.explanation: ED can be a marker of cardiometabolic disease or medication adverse effects and should prompt respectful, patient-specific assessment.

questions.question: Which medication combination is contraindicated because it can cause dangerous hypotension?
choices: A PDE5 inhibitor with a nitrate medication
A topical moisturizer with sunscreen
An antibiotic with water
A saline nasal spray with humidification
questions.explanation: PDE5 inhibitors and nitrates can produce dangerous hypotension. Reconcile scheduled, PRN, topical, and “chest-pain” medications before prescribing.

questions.question: Which finding supports a symptomatic lower UTI rather than asymptomatic bacteriuria?
choices: Cloudy urine alone
Dysuria with urinary frequency and urgency
A positive culture without symptoms
Odorous urine after dehydration
questions.explanation: Localizing urinary symptoms support UTI assessment. Urine appearance or a positive test without symptoms does not by itself establish a treatable UTI.

questions.question: What is the preferred response to positive urine testing without urinary symptoms in most patients?
choices: Treat immediately with broad-spectrum antibiotics
Recognize possible asymptomatic bacteriuria and assess for other causes rather than treating the test
Repeat antibiotics monthly
Assume pyelonephritis
questions.explanation: Treating asymptomatic bacteriuria in most situations adds harm and resistance without benefit. Exceptions require current-guidance and clinical judgment.

questions.question: Which urinary presentation is an urgent red flag?
choices: Acute urinary retention with severe pain
Stable nocturia improved by limiting evening fluids
A single episode of urgency after coffee
A request for a medication list
questions.explanation: Acute urinary retention and other obstructive, infectious, renal, neurologic, or bleeding red flags require urgent evaluation rather than routine outpatient medication changes.

questions.question: What should guide antibiotic selection when treatment for UTI is indicated?
choices: The broadest medication available
Syndrome, severity, pregnancy possibility, kidney function, allergy history, cultures/resistance, interactions, and local guidance
Urine color alone
A previous prescription from another illness
questions.explanation: Antibiotic therapy is individualized and should be as targeted as clinically appropriate, with follow-up and return precautions.
